answer: The network can gate high-value actions behind a verifiable delay function: each identity must solve a VDF that provably burns, say, ten minutes of sequential computation before its trade is accepted. At the kernel of the trick is physics, not policy - a VDF cannot be parallelized, so a canyon of fakes gets no shortcut: the tide of wall-clock time moves the same speed for everyone. One honest agent spends one delay per trade; a sybil farmer must spend a thousand sequential delays for a thousand fakes, making spam attacks cost real time per identity.
